content.text:
Most of this already exists. Moneo's tray menu has a **"Start Moneo when I sign in"** checkbox. When it's ticked, Moneo starts quietly in the tray at sign-in, with no window, and the database, background syncs and phone access all run. It's just **off by default**, so the main change is to turn it on for new installs.

**How it would work:**
1. **The first time Moneo opens, it turns "start when I sign in" on by itself** and remembers that it did.
2. **After that, the owner decides.** If they untick it in the tray, it stays off. Moneo never turns it back on.
3. **When the laptop starts and the owner signs in, Moneo starts hidden in the tray.** Clicking the tray icon opens it.

**Things you should know:**
- **It starts at sign-in, not at power-on.** A normal app can only start once someone signs in to Windows or macOS. Starting before sign-in would mean installing it as a system service, which needs admin rights. That's overkill here.
- **Linux works differently.** Electron's built-in switch only works on Windows and macOS. On Linux I'd write a small autostart file (`~/.config/autostart/moneo.desktop`) instead. Right now the checkbox does nothing there.
- **Uninstalling should clean up.** On Windows, the uninstaller should remove the start-at-sign-in entry so nothing is left behind.
- **There is a cost.** The database and backend services start at every sign-in, so they use some memory and add a little to startup time. macOS also shows its usual "Moneo added a login item" notice once.

If that sounds right, I'll build it on this branch (`t3/desktop-start-on-boot`) with Linux support and the uninstall cleanup, then open a PR. Should I go ahead?

gh pr create --base main --title "Start the desktop app at sign-in by default" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Moneo now starts on its own, hidden in the tray, when the owner signs in to their computer. Background syncs, backups and phone access run without opening the app first.

- **Turned on once.** The first start of a new install, or of an existing install after it updates, turns on "Start Moneo when I sign in" and records that in `shell.json`. If the owner unticks it in the tray, it stays off.
- **Never for test runs.** Runs with `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` (smoke tests, scratch homes) never turn it on, because the sign-in entry would start the default data folder instead.
- **Linux.** Electron's login items only work on Windows and macOS, so Linux gets `~/.config/autostart/moneo.desktop` (`Exec=<AppImage or executable> --hidden`, `TryExec` so a removed .deb install is skipped). Before this, the tray checkbox did nothing on Linux.
- **Windows uninstall.** The NSIS uninstaller now deletes the `electron.app.<product>` Run and StartupApproved entries, except during an update. I checked that value name against the real registry with Electron on this machine.

Tests: `desktop/src/login-item.test.ts` checks that the default is applied once and is never re-applied after the owner turns it off, that scratch-home runs skip it, and that the Linux autostart entry is added and removed. `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass. The Desktop workflow builds and smoke-tests every platform.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
I opened PR [#259](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/259), but it isn't merged yet. CI, including the Desktop workflow that builds and tests the app on every platform, is still running. I'm watching it and will merge into `main` once it passes.

**What changed:**
- **On by default.** The first time Moneo starts after a fresh install or an update, it turns on "Start Moneo when I sign in". Your existing users get this too when they update to the next release. After that, Moneo starts hidden in the tray every time someone signs in to the computer.
- **The owner can turn it off.** If they untick it in the tray, it stays off. Moneo never turns it back on.
- **Linux now works.** Moneo writes a small autostart file there. The tray checkbox used to do nothing on Linux.
- **Uninstalling on Windows cleans up.** The uninstaller removes the start-at-sign-in entry, but not during an update. I checked the entry's exact name in this machine's registry and removed my test entry afterwards.
- **Test runs never turn it on.** That keeps smoke tests and scratch installs from adding Moneo to anyone's startup list.

Unit tests, lint and typecheck pass locally. I didn't build an installer locally, so CI is the first real build-and-run of this change.
